subject: StreamLytics: customer-led load rehearsal — scheduling, allowlist, and k6 artifacts
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Hana Cho <hana@streamlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + next steps: load rehearsal planning

Hi Hana — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can lock in the customer-led load rehearsal: 

- Goal: Validate streaming concurrency SLO (95th pct latency < 250ms for single-stream responses; sustained throughput target 1200 reqs/min across 10 concurrent streams).
- Test tech: You mentioned running k6 for request-level traffic and a small Locust driver for multi-streams. We can accept either; we prefer k6 scripts for easier integration with our autoscaling telemetry.
- Required from StreamLytics: test account (API key/scoped), source IP ranges for allowlist, and a traffic profile (ramp, hold, users).

Proposed timeline:
1) Preflight dry-run (internal + short customer probe): July 22, 09:00–10:00 PDT
2) Full customer-led window (sustained traffic): July 25, 08:00–12:00 PDT

Can you confirm the windows or suggest alternatives? If those look good, can you share the IP ranges and the preferred k6 script (or we can provide a starter)?

I've attached a starter k6 script and our allowlist CSV template to speed things up.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Technical Account Manager — Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: k6_streamlytics_traffic_v2.js (script), redwood-allowlist-template.csv (csv template)

From: Hana Cho <hana@streamlytics.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@streamlytics.com>, ops@streamlytics.com
Date: 2028-07-15T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps: load rehearsal planning

Hi Sofia — thanks for the summary, that aligns with our expectations. Confirming windows look OK from our side; July 22 dry-run + July 25 full window works. A few clarifications: 

- Traffic shape: we'll do a 10min ramp to target, 3h steady hold at 1200 rpm, then 10min cool-down. We also plan a 10-user streaming test (each user opens a long-running websocket-like stream) to validate tail latency under concurrent KV cache pressure.
- SLO nuance: our internal product team cares about 99th pct tail for streaming messages (<600ms) in addition to your 95th request latency; please confirm Redwood's telemetry will capture stream-level percentiles.
- IP ranges: we'll provide a /24 and a secondary /25. Ops will send allowlist CSV with exact CIDRs.

We'll attach our ops contact and the k6 variant we have for earlier tests. If you prefer Redwood to run the k6 driver from our scripts, let us know credentials — otherwise we'll run from our CI and point to Redwood endpoints.

—Hana
Hana Cho
VP Product, StreamLytics
---
Attachments: streamlytics-k6-v1.js (customer script)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: ops@streamlytics.com, Hana Cho <hana@streamlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-16T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps: load rehearsal planning

Thanks Hana — great details. A few items from our preflight checklist and asks before the dry-run: 

- Allowlist: please attach the exact CIDRs in CSV (header: label,cidr). We'll import into our firewall rules and share the expected egress IPs for the Redwood test harness.
- Test account: we'll create a scoped API key for the rehearsal (limited to test model and quotas). Please confirm the redirect/callbacks are not required for this key.
- Telemetry: Redwood will expose per-stream and per-request percentiles (p50/p95/p99) in the Console; priyom will add a small dashboard tile for the stream-level p99 and tail-latency.
- Attachments: we'll iterate on your script — if you run from your CI that's fine; if you want Redwood to execute, we'll need a temporary SSH key + a runbook user with the test key.

Action items before July 22 dry-run: 
- StreamLytics: share IP csv, provide chosen method (Run from StreamLytics CI or Redwood-run).
- Redwood: generate test API key and a lightweight runbook (we'll add time-slots for teleconference).

Attaching a Redwood starter script and our allowlist template again — marissa will coordinate the runbook doc.

Cheers,
Sofia
---
Attachments: redwood-allowlist-template.csv, k6_streamlytics_traffic_v2.js

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@streamlytics.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Hana Cho <hana@streamlytics.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-16T16:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps: load rehearsal planning

Quick note from ops: attached is the allowlist CSV (streamlytics-ip-allowlist.csv). We'll run the k6 scripts from our CI; credentials below for the test account (we'll rotate post-test):

- Test API key: SL-TEST-xxxxxxxx (scoped to inference:test)
- Run method: StreamLytics CI -> will call Redwood hosted endpoint (region:us-west-2)

We also included minor edits to your starter k6 script to match our traffic generator. Confirm you've got the CIDRs and we'll expect the dry-run to start on the 22nd.

Alex
Ops Lead, StreamLytics

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Hana Cho <hana@streamlytics.com>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@streamlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps: load rehearsal planning

All set — we received the allowlist and test key, thanks Alex. Final prep notes and attendees for the dry-run on July 22 (09:00–10:00 PDT):

- Redwood attendees: Sofia (TAM), Marissa (Program Lead), Ben (SRE on-call), Priyom (perf engineer)
- StreamLytics attendees: Hana (product), Alex (ops), 2x platform engineers (ops@streamlytics.com)
- Objectives for dry-run: verify connectivity and allowlist, run a 15-min sanity k6 run at 200 rpm, validate telemetry ingestion and per-stream p99 tile.
- Success criteria to proceed to full window: connectivity OK, telemetry p99 visible, no auth errors, and Redwood logs show sustained token exchange errors <0.1% during the sanity run.

Link to runbook and live dashboard: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-StreamLytics-Runbook
HubSpot reference: HS-332751

We'll send calendar invites for both windows and include the runbook with step-by-step commands. Looking forward to the run.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Technical Account Manager — Redwood Inference
